clue.text: State doctor with first class return to W African republic

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: return here means the first-class pair is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or first class, the figure 1 serving as the letter I

explanation.surface: A medical man in a top-class compartment travels home to West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses the first-class pair, with the figure one read as the letter I; 'State' is a US state's postal code, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gambia is a small republic on the Atlantic coast of West Africa.

clue.text: Responsive to expert supporting' petitioner's final plea

indicators.note: in a down clue the word below holds up the one above, so supporting places expert underneath

parts.note: a prayer, a petition to God, ends with the word amen
someone able is skilled or expert

explanation.surface: Someone receptive to a specialist backing the last request of a person asking a favour.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' places the second piece beneath the first; the stray mark after the word is a print blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenable describes someone willing and open to persuasion or to a suggestion.

clue.text: Oatmeal perhaps makes us flourish

parts.note: oatmeal is an example of bran, the husk of cereal grain
a bowl of oatmeal porridge is a dish

explanation.surface: A healthy breakfast of porridge helps us to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oatmeal perhaps' supplies a whole phrase, BRAN DISH, read as one word; 'flourish' is the verb meaning wave about, not thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To wave a sword or stick about showily is to flourish it.

clue.text: It's true about getting the wind up concerning pensions

indicators.note: about means the word for true goes round the other piece

parts.note: actual means real or true

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for wind is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: air is wind, moving air

explanation.surface: Getting nervous about pension calculations is understandable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the wind word and 'about' wraps the true word round it; 'getting the wind up' suggests fear but is two separate signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Actuaries calculate risks and payouts for insurers and pension funds, so actuarial work relates to pension schemes.

clue.text: First novel

definitions.meaning: earliest, the one at the start

explanation.surface: The debut book by an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Original means earliest or first, and also new or fresh, as a novel idea is.

clue.text: Rows near the stage when the band plays for time

parts.note: an orchestra is a large band of musicians
to stall is to delay or play for time

explanation.surface: The front seats are filled while the musicians delay the start.
explanation.walkthrough: ORCHESTRA STALLS are the theatre seats on the ground floor nearest the stage, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In a British theatre the front seats on the ground floor, close to the stage, are known by this name.

clue.text: Old heavyweight champion who got stoned

definitions.text: Old heavyweight champion who got stoned

parts.words: Old heavyweight champion who got stoned
parts.note: reads like a boxer gone to seed on drugs, but refers to the Philistine giant champion felled by a sling stone

explanation.surface: A former boxing champion who took drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The giant of the Bible was the Philistines' champion, killed by David's sling stone; 'stoned' is not about drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Philistine giant in the book of Samuel was the army's champion fighter, struck down by a single pebble.

clue.text: Turned up musical information for film

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the whole run of letters is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber stage musical
gen is informal British for information

explanation.surface: Someone has unearthed details about a show for a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reverses EVITA plus GEN as a single run. A photographic negative is the developed film.
explanation.definitionFit: A developed photographic plate or strip with light and dark inverted is a negative, from which prints are made.

clue.text: This coastal region sounds dull

indicators.note: sounds means the word for dull is said aloud to give a near-identical sounding word

parts.note: literal can mean prosaic and unimaginative, dull

explanation.surface: The seaside area seems boring.
explanation.definitionFit: A littoral is the shore zone between land and sea.

clue.text: Rejected terms leading to contraction of meaning

indicators.note: leading to puts the first piece ahead of the next
rejected here means the word for terms is turned back to front

parts.note: names are terms, words for things
a tic is an involuntary muscle contraction

explanation.surface: Turned-down conditions produce a narrowing of sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' reverses NAMES to SEMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantic is the adjective for things relating to sense in language.

clue.text: Plant disease covering most of England

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the slang word is dropped

parts.note: Blighty is old soldiers' slang for Britain or England

explanation.surface: A crop sickness spreading over much of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: BLIGHTY is British army slang for home; 'most of' removes its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blight is a fungal disease that withers crops such as potatoes.

clue.text: We hear the female attendant is bespoke

indicators.note: we hear means the word for the female attendant is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a handmaid is a female servant or attendant

explanation.surface: A lady's maid is said to be made to order.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke items are made individually, often by hand, to a customer's order.

clue.text: Military entertainment containing untidy item and…

parts.note: tat is shabby, tasteless stuff, junk
too means also, and

explanation.surface: An army show includes a messy object, and the clue runs on to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots lead into 13, but this clue is complete. 'containing' links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is an evening military display of drumming and marching, like the Edinburgh one.

clue.text: … frivolous burlesque version of this

parts.note: a skit is a short comic burlesque or parody

indicators.note: version of means the word this appears in a rearranged form

explanation.surface: A light-hearted comic take on the previous clue's military show.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots tie this to 12: 'this' is the clue word itself, rearranged by 'version of' after the burlesque.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittish means flighty, lively and not serious.

clue.text: Silk producer located on the outskirts of London town

indicators.note: on the outskirts of means the word for located wraps round the town

parts.note: something set in a place is situated or located there
Pinner is a suburb in north-west London

explanation.surface: A silk mill is sited on the edge of a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinner is a suburb in north-west London; 'on the outskirts of' wraps the located word round it. Spiders and silkworms both have the silk-producing organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinneret is the organ through which a spider or silkworm extrudes its thread.

clue.text: Married? He's desperate to become engaged!

indicators.note: desperate signals the letters of the word before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A bachelor anxious to get engaged, though he may be married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate' scrambles the letters of He's; 'engaged' means gears interlocking, not betrothal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear teeth mesh when they interlock, becoming engaged.

clue.text: Mound supporting breakwater liable to enlargement

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting puts the mound piece below the breakwater piece

parts.note: a mole is a stone pier or breakwater
a hill is a raised mound of earth

explanation.surface: A heap of earth holds up a sea wall that is prone to growth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'make a mountain out of a molehill', exaggerating a trifle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of making a mountain out of one says this small heap is what people blow up into something bigger.

clue.text: Put stopper on squash

explanation.surface: Cork a bottle of fruit cordial.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppress is to stop or quell, and to crush a rebellion or a feeling.

clue.text: The Alchemist's remedy

indicators.note: the possessive is read as has, so the clue words have the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A magician's cure-all potion.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'The Alchemist'; 'remedy' is a verb meaning cure.
explanation.definitionFit: To heal is to cure or put right.

clue.text: The appropriate treatment to put someone under

definitions.text: The appropriate treatment to put someone under

parts.words: The appropriate treatment to put someone under
parts.note: reads like anaesthesia before surgery, but describes the method of putting a person into a trance

explanation.surface: The right procedure for anaesthetising a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' suggests general anaesthesia; here it means being in a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypnotist induces a trance state, putting the subject under their influence.

clue.text: A rook when fully grown coils round this

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook
mature means adult, fully grown

explanation.surface: A young bird which, once adult, wraps itself round something.
explanation.walkthrough: An armature is the core of an electric motor around which wire coils are wound.
explanation.definitionFit: In a motor or dynamo the iron core carrying the windings is the armature.

clue.text: Liberal assembly by the end of the day is in a weary way

indicators.note: assembly means the letters of the word Liberal are put together in a new order
the end of picks out the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A political party conference that drags on till nightfall leaves people tired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' rearranges LIBERAL to BLEARIL, then Y from 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blearily describes doing something with tired, unfocused eyes.

clue.text: Braw lad improvising with piercing instrument

indicators.note: improvising means the letters of the two words are made up afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A fine Scottish boy making do with a tool for boring holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Braw' is Scots for fine; 'improvising' rearranges BRAWLAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A bradawl is a small hand tool for making holes in wood.

clue.text: Recurring error I introduced is being discovered

indicators.note: introduced means the letter I is put inside the reversed word
recurring is read as running back, so the word for error is reversed

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: A repeated mistake I brought in is coming to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recurring' turns LAPSE into ESPAL, and 'introduced' inserts I.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is an old word for spying out or detection.

clue.text: Butcher wants one to cut joints

indicators.note: butcher, as a verb meaning mangle, says the letters of the next two words are hacked into a new order

explanation.surface: A butcher needs a tool for carving meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' looks like the person but is a verb rearranging WANTSONE; the joints are woodwork joints, not cuts of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: This small fine-toothed saw is used for cutting precise woodworking joints.

clue.text: O'Neill's cold caller

parts.note: refers to Eugene O'Neill's play The ... Cometh, the cold caller being the ice deliverer

explanation.surface: A salesman phoning unannounced.
explanation.walkthrough: A cold caller usually phones unannounced; here he delivers ice, in Eugene O'Neill's play.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who delivered blocks of ice door to door is the title figure of O'Neill's play.

clue.text: What fun to press a flower

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun, a spree
to spur is to urge or press on

explanation.surface: Pressing flowers is a jolly pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden plant with spikes of blue flowers.

clue.text: Lean without being limp

parts.note: to list is to lean to one side, as a ship does
less means lacking or without

explanation.surface: Thin but not floppy.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless means lacking energy, languid.

clue.text: Old sampler in a royal dining room

definitions.text: Old sampler in a royal dining room

parts.words: Old sampler in a royal dining room
parts.note: suggests antique embroidery hung on a palace wall, but describes the servant who tried food for poison

explanation.surface: An antique piece of needlework hanging in a palace dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: A sampler is also embroidery; here it is a person who samples the king's food.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal households once employed someone to try dishes first to check for poison.
